findings.title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is not awaited
findings.body: On booking cancel, request-reschedule (bookings.tsx around the workflowReminders.forEach), workflow update, and reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts), deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited. This PR removed the previously awaited prisma.workflowReminder deletes, so the only record that a reminder must not be sent is the cancelled flag (or row delete) inside those async functions. Next.js ends the request when the handler promise resolves, which drops in-flight work. If that update or delete never commits, the cron still treats the reminder as active and SendGrid/Twilio still deliver the cancelled or rescheduled booking email or SMS.

findings.title: immediateDelete bypasses the cancelled flag and does not retry
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., immediateDelete=true) posts a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking), workflow delete, and step delete all pass true. That is the same immediate scheduled_sends cancel the PR says fails once 100 cancellations are pending, and a failure is only logged. Because cancelled stays false/null, scheduleEmailReminders will never retry the cancel, so those emails are still sent. On success the orphaned row also remains until scheduledDate passes.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts every pending cancellation
findings.body: The cron loads every reminder with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within the next hour, then calls SendGrid and queues the row delete inside a single try around the whole loop. Deletes run only after every request succeeds. Any failure (null or stale referenceId, already-cancelled batch, rate limit) jumps to the catch, so no rows from that run are deleted and later reminders in the list are not cancelled. The next run hits the same already-cancelled or invalid batch first, throws again, and never reaches the rest. Those emails stay scheduled at SendGrid until send time, which is the original bug. Each reminder needs its own try/catch, a skip when referenceId is missing, and the row must be removed or left retryable even when SendGrid errors.

findings.title: Cron still schedules reminders that were cancelled but not yet sent
findings.body: After the cancel pass, unscheduled email reminders (scheduled=false, scheduledDate within 72 hours) are loaded with no filter on cancelled and no check that the booking is still ACCEPTED. Reminders that were never given a SendGrid referenceId are only removed by the un-awaited delete in deleteScheduledEmailReminder. If that delete does not commit, or a row is marked cancelled while still unscheduled, this loop creates a batch, sends the email, and sets scheduled=true. The scheduling query needs to exclude cancelled reminders and cancelled/rescheduled bookings before calling SendGrid.
